issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning a String (the textual message "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), but the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with return type boolean and the Goat and Seal implementations print the message and return true. This mismatch between the specified API (String) and the provided implementation (boolean) will confuse students about the expected return type and value, and prevents straightforward implementation following the UML/specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String, and update Goat and Seal to return the string message (e.g. "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Alternatively, if the boolean return was intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify boolean and adjust the descriptive text accordingly — but prefer making the interface return String to match the UML and textual requirements.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning a String (the message "[Animal Type] [name] is milked") and the provided Main template prints the result of m.messageOnMilk(). However, the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with a boolean return type and the implementations (Goat, Seal) print the message and return true. This mismatch between the expected String return and the solution's boolean return (and side-effect printing) breaks the conceptual mapping for students: they are instructed to implement/expect a String-returning method but the solution uses a differently-typed method with different behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement: change the Milkable interface to declare String messageOnMilk(), and update Seal and Goat to return the formatted String ("[Animal Type] [name] is milked") without printing inside the method. Let callers (e.g., Main or Farm) print the returned String. This makes the method signature and behavior consistent across problem, template, and solution.
